T: They may take our lives. They'll never take our shortbread.
D: A Scottish commoner leads a rebellion against the English king.
P: Serve the mains when Wallace rallies the army before Stirling.
S: Haggis (or lamb mince with oats, onion, allspice and pepper) rolled into balls, crumbed, fried at 175C until crisp, with a whisky and mustard cream dip.
food for a march across the Highlands
Oatcakes of oats, butter, salt and hot water rolled thin, baked at 180C for 20 minutes, with sharp Scottish cheddar and apple chutney.
Scottish smoked salmon on brown bread with lemon butter, dill and capers, cut into neat squares.
M: a pot over the fire in the Highlands
Lamb neck simmered 2 hours with pearl barley, split peas, leek, carrot and swede, the meat pulled back in, parsley on top. Crusty bread.
Highland venison with neeps and tatties
Venison backstrap seared to rare and rested, with mashed swede, buttery mashed potato and a whisky pepper sauce.
W: a tin of shortbread for the long march
Butter and sugar creamed, plain flour and a little rice flour worked in, pressed into a tin, pricked, baked at 150C for 40 minutes, cut while warm, caster sugar on top.
K: 30ml Scotch whisky in a small glass, a jug of cold water on the side to add a few drops.

s.note: food for a march across the Highlands
s.how: Mix 200g oats with 50g melted butter, salt and a splash of hot water. Roll thin, cut rounds and bake at 180C for 20 minutes. Serve with 200g sharp cheddar and apple chutney.
Mash 50g soft butter with lemon zest. Spread on 6 slices wholemeal bread and top with 200g smoked salmon, dill and capers. Cut into neat squares.

m.note: a pot over the fire in the Highlands
m.how: Simmer 1kg lamb neck in 2.5L water with 100g pearl barley and 100g split peas for an hour. Add 2 leeks, 2 carrots and a diced swede and simmer another hour. Pull the meat back in and finish with parsley. Serve with crusty bread.

w.note: a tin of shortbread for the long march
w.how: Beat 250g butter with 110g caster sugar, then work in 300g flour and 60g rice flour. Press into a tin, prick and bake at 150C for 40 minutes. Cut while warm and sprinkle with caster sugar.

d.how: Pour 30ml Scotch whisky into each of four small glasses. Put a jug of cold water on the side so everyone can add a few drops. Raise it to freedom.
